title: In a 2014-2019 Argo sample, ERSSTv6 warmed 0.047 C relative to profiles at the nearest grid cells
abstract: We tested the ERSSTv6 change near 2017 against direct Argo measurements across three ocean basins. We used the GDAC profile files for day 15 of every month in 2014-2019. We selected delayed-mode primary profiles, quality flag 1, and adjusted temperature at 3.5-6.5 dbar. The main matched test used 23,959 profiles from 5,839 floats in 337 ten-degree boxes. It compared 2017-2019 with 2014-2016, with fixed box and calendar-month means. ERSSTv6 minus Argo rose by 0.047 C (95 percent interval 0.008-0.087 C). ERSSTv5 minus Argo changed by -0.003 C (-0.041 to 0.036 C). Outside the tropical Pacific, the v6-minus-v5 change was 0.048 C (0.025-0.071 C), so the version change extends beyond the earlier mooring test. But the direct v6-minus-Argo change there was 0.047 C (-0.001 to 0.094 C). This primary regional test did not exclude zero. Bilinear sampling gave a smaller all-ocean sample change of 0.029 C (-0.014 to 0.072 C). Float-type subsets had different support and uncertain signs. These results support a version-specific warm change, but do not give one precise global correction or prove a common error in all basins. Argo is an ERSST input. A monthly product and one profile day per month have collocation error. The test does not find an abrupt break date or its cause. Code, source hashes, aggregate scores and figures support inspection and repetition.

display.caption: Matched changes from 2014-2016 to 2017-2019. Intervals include spatial and temporal dependence. Values refer to the sampled support.
Sensitivity to sampling, depth, float type, spatial resolution and error controls. Different tests have different support.
Monthly residuals and six-month means after fixed box and calendar-month means are removed.

We extend its mooring comparison to direct Argo profiles across three basins. The change outside the tropical Pacific is clearer between versions than against the profiles.
